evidence_quotes.quid_pro_quo: Rep said 'that could take ten to fifteen minutes' and asked 'Is this a good time to talk about your move?' but did not frame a dependable quote promise and did not wait for explicit yes before launching into address confirmation.
evidence_quotes.discovery_basics: Name (Ashley), moving day (October 4th), pickup (1640 ET C, Adjuster Boulevard, Houston 77008) and destination (5114 West Lacey garden loop, Houston 77018) confirmed; apartment type and size gathered.
evidence_quotes.their_agenda: Rep asked 'But aside from this ma'am, do you have any other concerns about the moving process?' — but this came after substantial probing (property type, floor, distance, special items, TV size, appliances, destination details, access concerns).
evidence_quotes.two_layers_deep: Customer raised multi-stop concern (drop-off at mother-in-law's apartment, then main destination). Rep dug in: 'are we only dropping off one couch?' and got specifics (one couch, two dressers), then confirmed full three-location sequence back to customer.
evidence_quotes.logistics_details_gathered: Property type (1BR apartment and 2-story house), floors/stories (second floor stairs, two story destination), access (stairs only, parking/street parking), distances (parking to stairs, stairs to apt, driveway available), special items (60-inch TV), boxes (acknowledged 15–25 range, customer said less), additional stops (mother-in-law's first-floor apartment).
evidence_quotes.box_count_asked: Rep offered typical range: 'Normally for a one bedroom apartment we see fifteen to 25 boxes. Do you think you would fall within that range?'
evidence_quotes.estimate_anchor: Rep gave range: '3 hours to 4 hours' and hourly rate ($96/hour per mover, $192 total, 2.5-hour minimum), but stated estimate as '$5.76277 million' (apparent transcript error or verbal slip), not a personalized range tied to customer's specific multi-stop logistics.
evidence_quotes.pricing_framing: Fully present: hourly rate structure ($96/mover, $192 for two movers), no hidden fees (gas, truck, taxes, insurance, wraps, pads, tools all included, no sterile/disassemble/reassemble/transportation fees), 2.5-hour minimum, 15-minute increments after minimum.
evidence_quotes.feels_fair_then_silence: Not asked. Rep moved directly to availability: 'We actually have availability on Sunday, October 4th in the morning. A thirty to 9:00 AM is the arrival window. Would you like to reserve your schedule for this Sunday?'
evidence_quotes.final_concerns_check: Not asked. Rep moved from booking confirmation directly to closing: 'So if everything is good then we're good to go. But then if you have any more questions or concern just reply back to that email.'
evidence_quotes.explicit_ask: Never asked. Rep presented availability and asked 'Would you like to reserve your schedule for this Sunday?' (booking window question), but never asked the core close: 'Would you like our help with your move?' or equivalent.
evidence_quotes.booking_confirmed: Partial. Confirmed date (October 4th), time window (8:30–9:00 AM), unit numbers (1021 and 714), and stated confirmation email will have date, time, addresses, contact info — but did not confirm phone number, crew size (stated as 2 movers but never confirmed), or crew notes about customer concerns (multi-stop, second-floor stairs access).

top_strength: Rep thoroughly probed logistics for a multi-location move (apartment with stairs, mother-in-law drop-off, destination house) and dug two layers deep into the customer's stated concern, capturing all specifics and confirming the three-stop sequence back to the customer.
coaching_note: Section 2 (Their Agenda) came after probing had already started, Section 4 ('Does that feel fair?') was never asked, Section 5 (Two Promises) were completely skipped, Section 6 (final concerns check) was not asked, and Section 7 never included the explicit ask for the business ('Would you like our help with your move?') — rep jumped straight to booking-window questions instead.
